page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-80 is a compute-focused instance configured with 80 virtual CPUs and 80 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 40 physical cores across 80 hardware threads. The processor features 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Vector processing includes baseline AVX support, though newer instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX are absent. Standard hardware acceleration extensions for cryptography, including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, are supported.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute performance across multi-threaded applications. The server achieves top-quartile performance in stress-ng multi-core testing (107,952.86) and PassMark CPU score (69,646.99), alongside elevated throughput in PassMark encryption (85,363.22) and Clang software compilation (43,413.0). In-memory database workloads also perform strongly, with Redis SET throughput measuring 77.49 million operations per second and PassMark database operations scoring in the top 25%. However, single-core benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core (1,463.0) and single-threaded gzip compression, perform in the middle 50% range, reflecting the frequency profile typical of high-density AMD EPYC server chips.

The instance does not include bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent disk needs rely entirely on attached cloud block storage. Similarly, it lacks discrete GPU acceleration and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The 1 GB per core memory allocation restricts use with memory-hungry applications, but it offers high core density and computational cost efficiency for CPU-bound tasks where large RAM buffers are unnecessary.

Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-80 is suited for batch processing, CI/CD compilation pipelines, distributed code build farms, ray tracing tasks, and CPU-intensive compute workloads that scale across high thread counts without substantial memory overhead.
